inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated cash-flow statement 'Share-based payment expenses' 63,839 (6098.T_Annual_FY2025.txt:1487); FY2026 guided 78.9bn (Q1 FY2026 Tanshin). No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (awards are delivered from BIP/ESOP trust shares), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.fy0_note: Recruit labels fiscal years by the April start year: FY2025 = 1 Apr 2025 - 31 Mar 2026. FY2026 (Apr 2026 - Mar 2027) is the guidance year and forecast year 1.
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 1,472,504,149 less treasury 80,332,780 (35.5m held directly + 44.8m in BIP/ESOP trusts) = 1,392.17m at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY2026 Tanshin), plus ~8.97m dilutive potential shares (stock options 1.48m + BIP 2.92m + ESOP 4.57m, FY2025 diluted-EPS table) = 1,401.1m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged. Buybacks since 30 Jun 2026 (JPY 350bn / 64m-share programme running to 30 Nov 2026) are ignored on both sides: they reduce the count and the cash pile together.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the statements and the flows: 10y JGB ~1.7% (Nov 2026), 6.0% equity risk premium (Japan ~5.5% plus a global-exposure increment), beta ~1.15 for a cyclical global HR marketplace -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Borrowings are JPY 0.7bn against JPY 853bn cash, so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the JFTC matter and AI disintermediation are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate (charge risk once). Roughly half of EBITDA+S is USD-earned; FX translation is a scenario risk (guidance assumes 159 JPY/USD; spot 158.4 on 2026-11-07), not a discount-rate adjustment.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost, consistent with Recruit's own EBITDA+S definition, which does NOT add back right-of-use depreciation (operating income + D&A excluding ROU depreciation + SBC). ROU depreciation (FY2025 37,050 = 107,077 total D&A - 70,027 ex-ROU) is therefore already inside the EBITDA+S margin path. The remainder of the cash lease cost - principal repaid 47,174 plus lease interest ~6,005 (interest paid; borrowings are negligible) less the 37,050 already charged = 16,129 = 0.44% of revenue - is charged via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.45%. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use (1.9%), so cash-tax EBIT does not charge the lease twice. Lease liabilities (JPY 178,169m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bonds/borrowings only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY 13,024m (30 Jun 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; NCI share of profit is ~0.1bn/yr so the consolidated flows are not adjusted.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income FY2025 16,587 (KPI InterestIncome; finance income 34,708 also carries FX and fair-value items that are largely non-cash). Stripped because net cash (853bn) is >1x the owner-FCF base; the cash pile is the matching asset in the bridge. Other financial assets (current 79,326 + non-current 140,242 at 30 Jun 2026 - time deposits, FVOCI equity instruments, associates) are NOT added to the bridge because the quarterly does not break out their composition; a conservative omission worth up to ~JPY 157/share at book.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route), 10-year horizon, probability-weighted. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a standard operating company (HR marketplace + staffing + Japanese vertical media); first valuation of this ticker, no prior model to match. owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied for: JPY-built WACC, single lease treatment (B), NCI in bridge, interest-income/matching-asset rule. last_fcf = reported_fcf 607,140 (OCF 669,431 - capex 62,291) - SBC 63,839 - interest income 16,587 - lease principal 47,174 = 479,540 (treatment B deducts the lease cash from the flows). Owner-FCF history for CAGRs uses the same four-term adjustment from FY2019 (IFRS 16 adoption) onward. Buyback_cash 678,754 is actual FY2025 financing outflow (annual CF statement line 1510); the flat count is funded, not a convention. EBITDA definition: FY2021+ EBITDA/EBITDA+S adds back SBC; the margin path below is on the EBITDA+S basis (FY2025 21.5%, FY2026 guided 26.1% = 1,105/4,230) and SBC is then deducted explicitly. Regime caution: FY2026 guidance was raised in August 2026 (revenue 4,030 -> 4,230bn, EBITDA+S 949 -> 1,105bn) almost entirely on Indeed US ARPJ pricing, with US job-posting volume still guided down; the base case therefore lets the blended margin ease from 26.1% to 25.0% over FY2027-FY2029 rather than extrapolating Q1's 28%.

equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2026 Tanshin balance sheet, 30 Jun 2026

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: segment-weighted mid-term revenue growth (HR Technology high-single-digit, Staffing 2-3%, Marketing Matching 5-7%) after the FY2026 guidance year; the equity CAGR is meaningless here because JPY 1.5tn of buybacks shrank book value
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR -0.9% vs EPS 3yr CAGR +27.6% and revenue 3yr CAGR +2.5%: equity is distorted by FY2024-FY2025 buybacks (JPY 1,503bn combined) and EPS by the 9% share-count reduction, so neither is a growth anchor. FY2025 revenue (+3.9%) was also depressed by the RGF Staffing UK divestment and FX.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal: FY2020 179,676; FY2022 224,655; FY2025 479,540. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (28.8%) exceeds reported FCF (18.9%) because SBC fell from 72.7bn (FY2022) to 63.8bn and interest income fell from 18.8bn to 16.6bn over the window - the reverse of the usual SBC-outgrowing-cash warning. The 5-year figures start from COVID-depressed FY2020 and overstate trend; the FY2026 guidance year (+14.4% revenue, +39% EBITDA+S) is a pricing step-change on Indeed US, not the steady state.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = August-2026 revised guidance (4,230bn, +14.4%; Q1 printed +18.9%, so the remaining three quarters imply ~13% at 159 JPY/USD). Thereafter a segment-weighted blend: HR Technology high-single-digit as ARPJ gains annualise and volumes stay flat, Staffing (45% of revenue) 2-3% in a shrinking temp-staffing TAM, Marketing Matching 5-7%; decelerating to 2.5% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 at the guided 26.1% EBITDA+S margin (HR Technology 45.8%, Staffing 5.6%, MMT 30.0%). FY2027-FY2029 eases to 25.0% on the assumption that part of the Indeed US ARPJ step-up is competed or pushed back (LinkedIn, AI-native entrants) while US posting volumes stay soft; recovers to 25.5% by year 8 purely on mix as HR Technology outgrows Staffing. Q1's 28.0% is treated as a seasonal/pricing peak, not a run-rate.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2026 guided 78.9bn = 1.87% of 4,230bn; glides to 1.70% as HR Technology SBC (~USD 470m) grows slower than revenue.
base.tax_rationale: Book ETR 22.9% FY2025 / 22.6% FY2024; cash taxes paid 19.1% of FY2025 pre-tax profit (timing lag on rising profits). Ramped to 24% - above the book rate - because the US (21% federal + state) share of profit is rising and the Japanese statutory rate is ~30.6%.
base.capex_wc_rationale: Capex 1.8% of revenue (FY2025 1.68%, FY2024 1.84%, FY2023 2.05%; PP&E + intangibles/software) roughly equal to D&A ex-ROU at maturity. Working capital -3% of the revenue change: Staffing receivables grow with revenue and outweigh HR Technology's modest deferred revenue; FY2025 OCF (669bn) ~= NI + D&A + SBC (668bn), so the net drag is small.

bull.narrative: Guidance beaten again in FY2026 (16% revenue growth: ARPJ gains compound with a late-FY2026 US hiring recovery), Indeed's pricing power proves durable, the ChatGPT distribution deal and Career Scout/Talent Scout agents make Indeed the AI-era hiring layer rather than its victim, and HR Technology mix lifts the blended margin to 28.5% by FY2030. Terminal growth 3.0% reflects the USD-earning majority of profit.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands below the raised guide (11% growth: H2 US volumes roll over as JOLTS 'high openings, low hiring' turns to falling openings, and the yen firms toward 150). FY2027-FY2028 is a US hiring recession: employers push back on ARPJ, postings fall, AI-mediated search (ChatGPT, agent marketplaces) erodes Indeed's discovery traffic and forces further restructuring, and the blended margin falls to 19.5% - roughly the FY2022-FY2023 level of 16-18% EBITDA ex-SBC plus the SBC add-back. The JFTC fee-fixing case against Recruit Staffing ends in a surcharge of order JPY 40bn, taken as ~1pp of FY2027 margin. SBC stays elevated as a share of a smaller revenue base. Recovery to a 22% margin and 2.5% growth, with the terminal multiple capped at 15x for a cyclical that has just shown its downside.

scenario_narratives.base: Recruit delivers the August-2026 FY2026 guide (revenue JPY 4,230bn, EBITDA+S JPY 1,105bn) on Indeed US pricing, then growth settles to a mid-single-digit, segment-weighted blend: HR Technology high-single-digit with US posting volumes flat, Staffing 2-3%, Marketing Matching 5-7%. The blended EBITDA+S margin eases from 26.1% to 25.0% through FY2029 as part of the ARPJ step-up is competed away and the AI transition carries product cost, then recovers to 25.5% on mix. Cash tax ramps to 24%, SBC glides from 1.87% to 1.70% of revenue, buybacks keep the diluted count flat at 1,401m. The JFTC matter is treated as a low-probability cost not in the base flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Indeed's ARPJ gains prove durable and compound with a US hiring recovery from late FY2026; the ChatGPT distribution partnership and Career Scout/Talent Scout agents make Indeed the hiring layer of AI search rather than its casualty; Europe/Others HR Technology keeps growing double digits and HR Technology mix lifts the blended margin to 28.5% by FY2030. Revenue grows 16% in FY2026 and 9%/8%/7% thereafter; terminal growth 3.0% on the USD-earning majority of profit.
scenario_narratives.bear: The ARPJ-led acceleration reverses: a US hiring recession in FY2027-FY2028 cuts posting volumes while employers push back on per-posting price, AI-mediated job discovery erodes Indeed's traffic economics, the yen firms, and Recruit Staffing pays a JFTC surcharge of order JPY 40bn. Revenue is flat then -3%, the blended margin troughs at 19.5%, SBC rises as a share of revenue, and the business recovers only to a 22% margin and 2.5% growth, capitalised at a 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because (1) profit growth is now concentrated in one segment and one metric (Indeed US ARPJ) with US posting volumes still guided down - a single-lever acceleration is also single-lever to reverse; (2) the JFTC on-site inspection of Recruit Staffing (June 2026) is a live, unquantified regulatory liability explicitly excluded from guidance; (3) generative-AI disintermediation of job-board discovery is a structural, not cyclical, risk and the ~1,300 Indeed/Glassdoor role cuts show the transition is real. Bull lowered from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs several independent things to go right - durable pricing power, a US hiring recovery, the AI-agent strategy monetising, and a weak yen - and because the shares have already nearly tripled off the 52-week low, so the beat-and-raise pattern is at least partly priced. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Recruit as a stream of owner free cash flow - after SBC, after the full cash cost of leases, excluding interest on the JPY 853bn cash pile (which is added back once in the bridge) - built from components off the FY2026 guidance year and a segment-weighted deceleration, discounted at a JPY-built 8.5% cost of equity. The FY2026 step-up is treated as a pricing event on Indeed US whose durability is the central uncertainty, so the base margin path gives some of it back before mix restores it, and the scenario weights lean toward the downside. The house figure (SBC expensed) is the headline; the street figure (SBC as non-cash, the convention behind 'EBITDA+S') is reported as the top of the accounting band.
key_risks_to_valuation: Durability of Indeed US ARPJ pricing: the FY2026 guidance raise (EBITDA+S 949 -> 1,105bn) is almost entirely price, with US posting volume still guided down; employer pushback or LinkedIn/AI-native competition would reverse it quickly
US labour-market cycle: HR Technology US is the largest and highest-margin profit pool and is highly correlated with JOLTS openings, which were cooling through late 2026
Generative-AI disintermediation of job-board discovery (ChatGPT job search, agentic hiring) and the unproven monetisation of Indeed's own AI agents
JFTC antitrust investigation into Recruit Staffing (fee-fixing with four peers): unquantified surcharge and reputational exposure, excluded from guidance
FX: roughly half of EBITDA+S is USD/EUR-earned; guidance assumes 159 JPY/USD and a yen appreciation cycle would mechanically lower yen-reported growth
Staffing (45% of revenue) is in a structurally shrinking temporary-staffing TAM at 5-6% margins

Terminal-value dependence: a long-duration, net-cash compounder at an 8.5% discount rate puts most of the value in the terminal; the sensitivity grid and required-return table show how steeply value falls with the rate

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular TSE close); 52-week range 6,040-19,560. USD/JPY spot 158.4 (Yahoo USDJPY=X, 2026-11-07) used only to sanity-check the 159 guidance assumption.
